Resolves #19810

> 🌿 A timed-out stack return used to say only that no claim came; what became unsayable is "the red is in CI and nobody can tell from the log which side went quiet".

Three CI heads failed scene 5's second take with the same empty snapshot (`claimCount 0`, no preview, no indicators), one of them a grid-only change, and the trace carried no page console: the proof named the vessel's side and nothing of main's. `readCrossWindowGestureSnapshot` now describes, on every unready read, the surfaces a claim would have crossed — the participation and its target, the coordinator's claim and hover state, the source zone's arming, both windows' inner rects and this source's native ownership records — as `claimSurfaces`; a ready read is unchanged, so the beat logs and receipts the e2e scenes compare stay byte-identical. `executeStackReturnStep`'s timeout proof adds the aimed return node and rect on its existing line, and the scene's assertion message already prints the proof, so the next CI red carries its cause.

Evidence: L2 (unit on the snapshot mixin + scenes 4 and 5 headless on the author's seat) → L2 required (AC-1, AC-2: the proof's shape and its print are unit- and spec-visible; the CI red itself is the consumer). Residual: none, Residual-Owner: none.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; baseline jobs ran.

## AC Evidence
| AC-1 the timeout proof names main's participation state and both windows' rects | `Workspace.spec.mjs` "an unready pointer read names the claim surfaces it crossed; a ready read carries none": the unready snapshot carries `claimSurfaces.participation`, `.coordinator` (arbiter claimCount/token/winner, active target zone, native hover and arbiter window ids), `.sourceZone`, `.windows.main/source.innerRect` and `.owners`; the ready read has no such field |
| AC-2 scene 5's failure message prints that proof | `WorkstationFiveBeatNL.spec.mjs:3165–3173` prints `remoteSnapshot` in the assertion message unchanged; the snapshot now carries `claimSurfaces` when unready, and the driver's proof adds `aimed: {nodeId, rect}` |

## Deltas from ticket
The ticket placed the description in `executeStackReturnStep`; it lives in `CrossWindowGestureSnapshot#describeClaimSurfaces` instead, because that mixin owns the reads (`Prescription checked: apps/workstation/view/CrossWindowGestureSnapshot.mjs — owns the concern`), and because `NativeGestureDriver.mjs` sits at its File Size Guard baseline (1238) and must not grow for a receipt. The ticket's leaf 2 (the fix) is a follow-up filed from the first CI red that carries this proof; the ticket body says so.

## Test Evidence
`unit/apps/workstation/Workspace.spec.mjs` + `GestureDriver.spec.mjs` green locally; `WorkstationFiveBeatNL.spec.mjs` scenes 4 and 5 green headless on the author's seat (the instrumented path only fires on an unready read, which a passing run never leaves behind). `check-file-sizes -b origin/dev` passes with the driver at 1238.

## Post-Merge Validation
- [ ] The next `e2e-brain (10/10)` red on scene 5 prints `remoteSnapshot.claimSurfaces` and `aimed` in the failure message; the cause gets named on #19810's follow-up from that log.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

- **Challenge**: Non-blocking observation on `aimed` visibility in Scene 5's failure output vs Scene 4's. `NativeGestureDriver.mjs:814` adds `aimed: {nodeId: returnNodeId ?? null, rect: returnRect ?? null}` to `returnResult.proof` alongside `remoteSnapshot`, and the PR body's `## Post-Merge Validation` notes that the next Scene 5 CI red prints `remoteSnapshot.claimSurfaces` and `aimed`. While Scene 4's assertion (`WorkstationFiveBeatNL.spec.mjs:2866`) serializes `JSON.stringify(result.proof)` in full (which includes `aimed`), Scene 5's assertion (`WorkstationFiveBeatNL.spec.mjs:3149–3157`) constructs an explicit 7-key object `{sourceArm, closeReceipt, phaseOrder, remoteSnapshot, sourceItemIds, sourceWindowGone, transfer}` that prints `remoteSnapshot` (including `remoteSnapshot.claimSurfaces`) but omits `aimed: returnResult.proof?.aimed`. Because both #19810 ACs are satisfied by `remoteSnapshot.claimSurfaces` printing in Scene 5's assertion message, this does not block merge; when the #19810 follow-up fix ticket is opened or `WorkstationFiveBeatNL.spec.mjs` is next touched, adding `aimed: returnResult.proof?.aimed` at `WorkstationFiveBeatNL.spec.mjs:3150` will expose `aimed` in Scene 5's failure log as well.
